quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Distracted drivers have a higher crash risk when using which of the following?
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players can all distract you while driving. This increases your risk of crashing.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey first?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions come before signs, signals, and road markings. Other people who can direct traffic include fire police, highway work flaggers, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, driving with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is illegal. Driving under the influence is dangerous and against the law.

questions.question: You may drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road:

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you sit in the back seat.
If you sit in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road. You also cannot have an open container of alcohol in the driver or passenger area.

questions.question: If your tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Do not slam on the brakes right away.
Slowly slow down and pull to the side of the road.

questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, release the gas and do not brake hard right away. Gradually slow down and gently apply the brakes before pulling to the side of the road.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the road ahead is a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs show:
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you of railroad crossings. You must yield to trains and not try to beat them across the tracks.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means slow down and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen because drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down so the other driver has enough space to pass. This lets them finish passing faster and more safely.

questions.question: When you approach an accident scene, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.

questions.explanation: Do not stop unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to an accident just to look.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot whenever you move your vehicle. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers did not see motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians. They are small, move fast, and have less noticeable lights. Stay alert to protect these vulnerable road users.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when the road is clear.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "be careful." Slow down, look around, and proceed with care.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Which one has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car whose driver honks first.

questions.explanation: When two cars reach an intersection at the same time with no traffic control, you must yield to the vehicle from the right.

questions.question: What greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?
questions.explanation: High speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle will hit if you crash.

questions.question: What should you do while backing up?

options.text: Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head and look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Leaving the car running while sitting in the driveway.

questions.explanation: Quick stops waste fuel because you must accelerate again to reach traffic speed. Look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Reduce speed when approaching a yield sign. Be prepared to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: Hurricane evacuation route signs:

options.text: Mark highways to use during a hurricane evacuation.
Only appear when there is a hurricane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mark highways to use during a hurricane evacuation.
questions.explanation: Hurricane evacuation route signs show which highways are emergency evacuation routes. Know where these signs are in your area in case you need to evacuate.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or drop back so they can see your vehicle.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Return to your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your mirror.

questions.question: When traffic lights are horizontal, the green light is:
questions.explanation: Some cities use horizontal traffic lights instead of vertical ones. On these signals, red is on the left, yellow is in the middle, and green is on the right.

questions.question: In snowy weather, what should happen to your following distance?
questions.explanation: In bad weather, slow down and increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. It takes longer to stop on icy roads than on dry roads.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes display arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A green arrow:

options.text: Is only used on one-way streets.
Means you may go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
Only applies if a green circular light is also showing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means you may go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow works like a green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, other drivers must prepare for:

options.text: The longer stopping distance that large vehicles need.
The shorter stopping distance that large vehicles need.
The lower noise from large vehicles.
The higher speed of large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance that large vehicles need.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop. Stay in places where the truck driver can see you and where large vehicles do not block your view of traffic.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one of the tracks is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before moving.
questions.explanation: Do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before crossing. Even with only one track, check again for another train coming.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires cannot clear water from the road as well. If you go too fast, your tires lose grip and your vehicle slides on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: When should you use a three-point turnabout?

options.text: Only when the street is too narrow for a U-turn and you cannot go around the block.
When driving on a one-lane, one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when the street is too narrow for a U-turn and you cannot go around the block.
questions.explanation: A three-point turnabout is difficult and dangerous. Use it only when the road is too narrow for a safe U-turn and you cannot go around the block. Use this turn only on a two-lane road.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The 35 mph speed limit starts at the next sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down.
You should go 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to slow down. The new speed limit shown on the sign begins at that sign.

questions.question: Round signs warn drivers of:
questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers of an upcoming railroad crossing. Drive with extra caution near these signs.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic from both directions cannot cross it to pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Taking drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the risk of a crash.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter) can harm your brain function and driving ability. Mixing alcohol with drugs greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: A good rule for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases crash risk. If you drive faster than others, you will keep passing. Drive with traffic flow, within the speed limit, and pass only as needed.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they:

options.text: Will drive the same as usual.
Can drive faster because they are more alert.
Should calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Should call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Emotions like worry, anger, or sadness distract you from driving because your mind is elsewhere. Calm down and focus on driving before you start the engine.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.
